meta.method: Extended the worker collectOH hook to return the FULL production indirect candidate set (OH near backbone at reaction events + survivors) = 2,307,782 positions. Validation: scored against the full 21x21 grid -> ratio 5.71 (indirect 191), reproducing the production 5.74 (E33, indirect 201). validation.note: The full-encounter OH set reproduces the production ratio -> it IS the production indirect model.

decomposition.note: Ratio across indirect-model x geometry (grid vs folded chromatin).

finding: The out-of-band production ratio (5.74) is dominated by the INDIRECT MODEL, not geometry. The encounter model (OH scored near a backbone throughout its lifetime) yields 2.3M candidates -> the per-sugar hit 1-(1-0.13)^k SATURATES, so the indirect count tracks the DNA in the track core regardless of fold. Folding drops the RAW OH capture (19.0->14.9) but saturation absorbs it, leaving the ratio geometry-insensitive (dR=1.04). Under the survival model (OH near backbone at 1us only) the ratio is 2.12 (in band) and folding DOES lower it (dR=0.716) - but that is a different, more restrictive indirect model.
implication: Reaching PARTRAC's 2-3 band is an INDIRECT-MODEL question, not a geometry one. This corrects E34's 'geometry is the keystone' framing: geometry (folding) is a ~28% lever ONLY under the survival model; under the actual production (encounter) model it is a red herring (dR~=1.0). The Geant4-DNA-faithful fix is to make DNA an EXPLICIT IRT reactant (OH + 2-deoxyribose -> SSB as a reaction channel, P~0.13 Nikjoo), so an OH damages a sugar only when it actually reacts WITH it - which the encounter proxy over-counts (OH consumed by OTHER radicals near a backbone) and the survival proxy under-counts (misses OH that reacted with the sugar mid-timeline). Neither current proxy matches Geant4's explicit reaction channel.
status: pass - decisive: indirect-model saturation (not geometry) drives the out-of-band ratio; the definitive Geant4-level fix is an explicit OH+DNA IRT reaction channel, not realistic geometry.
